name: Harbona
overview: Harbona was a male eunuch who served in the presence of King Ahasuerus as one of seven such officials. His role placed him in a position of trusted service within the royal court. Scripture does not provide information about his tribal affiliation or other personal details.
namesAndTitles: The name Harbona, also rendered Harbonah, means 'donkey driver.' This proper name likely reflects a functional or occupational designation rather than a divine naming, as it was not given by God. Both forms of the name appear in the book of Esther.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Harbona beyond his role as one of the seven eunuchs serving King Ahasuerus. There are no additional relational details provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Harbona's significance lies in his service within the Persian royal court during the reign of King Ahasuerus, as recorded in the book of Esther. His presence among the king's eunuchs highlights the structured and trusted nature of the king's household officials. Though details are limited, his role contributes to the broader narrative context of Esther's story.
